  PROBLEM: The activity check can use a stale session-page timestamp for a page-listed checker, causing it to be restarted even if it re-armed or started a stage after the page was read.
  WHY: `lookups_needed()` skips page-listed checkers, so `decide()` uses their page snapshot rather than a fresh `get_session` result; severity disagreement: deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro and qwen_qwen3_7-plus rate this NIT, while minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, and z-ai_glm-5_2 rate it MAJOR.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: PR title / description / README claim "keep a checker that itself ran in the last 90 minutes"
  expected_change_site: scripts/claude_checker_restart.py lines 652-658 (new condition 4 sub-check) plus the supporting `lookups_needed()` skip rule at lines 511-519; supporting test coverage in tests/test_claude_checker_restart.py around line 290.
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The new check uses the page's `updated_at` for page-listed checkers; `lookups_needed()` skips `get_session` for them (line 518) and `decide()` ignores any lookup that arrives (line 589). The two new tests cover the page-stale-`updated_at`-within-window case and the not-on-page case, but no test exercises a checker that IS on the page with `updated_at` already outside the 90-minute window — the live scenario the PR description cites. README line 1293-1299, agents.md line 295-298, and changelog.d/4910-restart-dead-checkers.md line 18 all describe the behaviour as "the checker's own last turn counts / ran in the last 90 minutes is kept" without the page-staleness qualifier that AD-17's chosen option A actually leaves.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:652-657 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new `_is_active` check uses the `view` timestamp from the session page snapshot for page-listed checkers, and `lookups_needed()` skips checker IDs already on the page (line 518: `if checker in on_page`), so `decide()` never calls `get_session` to refresh them.
  WHY: A checker whose snapshot `updated_at` is outside the 90-minute window but that actually re-armed or started a stage in the seconds between the page read and `decide()` could be restarted; the gap is unlikely for a healthy checker, and the PR's documented AD-17 tradeoff accepts it.

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:652-657 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The check can use a stale timestamp for a checker listed on the page, so the new guard does not cover activity after the page was read.
  WHY: If a listed checker re-arms or starts a stage after the session and trigger snapshots were read, the snapshots omit that activity; because `lookups_needed()` skips that checker, `decide()` uses its old `updated_at` and may restart it despite its recent activity, creating a duplicate check-in or stage.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:511-531, 652-658 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: For a checker ON the session page, `view` is the page snapshot. If the checker re-armed after the page was read, the page has the old `updated_at`, so `_is_active(view, now)` returns False.
  WHY: The test `test_condition_4_a_looked_up_checker_that_handed_off_after_the_page_is_kept` tests a looked-up checker, not a page-listed checker; the practical impact is low because the page is read recently and the live case (#4723) is NOT an example of this scenario.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:652-657 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The fix adds a `_is_active(view, now)` check to keep a checker that "ran in the window," but for page-listed checkers `view` is the stale page snapshot.
  WHY: `lookups_needed()` (line 518: `if checker in on_page ... continue`) skips page-listed checkers, so `get_session` is never called to refresh them, and `decide()` (line 589: `if checker in by_id: continue`) ignores any lookup result for a page-listed checker; a stale timestamp can cause the checker to be restarted and create a duplicate check-in or stage.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
